name: shopify-plus
_readme: Shopify Plus as a migration TARGET only. Seed from general platform knowledge; everything in research-seed.md is a hypothesis until verified with a shopify.dev URL and a date. No as_source: a Plus store is a multi-tenant SaaS whose extension points are themes, apps, extensions and Functions - there is no inspectable shop code base of the kind the scanner needs.

as_target.default_frontend: Online Store 2.0 Liquid theme (Dawn as reference theme); Hydrogen (React) on Oxygen for headless

snippets.critic2_persona: senior solution architect who has delivered many Shopify Plus programmes, is Shopify-certified, and knows the current Storefront/Admin API versions, Checkout Extensibility, Shopify Functions, B2B on Shopify and Markets in detail - including what requires an app and what is plan-gated
snippets.docs_domains: shopify.dev (Storefront API and Admin API GraphQL reference with the API-version selector, Shopify Functions, Checkout UI extensions, theme/Liquid and Online Store 2.0 sections, Hydrogen/Oxygen, rate limits), shopify.dev/changelog (breaking changes and API version release notes), help.shopify.com (merchant-facing docs: B2B on Shopify, Markets, Flow, Launchpad, plan limits). Always state the API version (YYYY-MM) a claim belongs to - a GraphQL field can exist in one version and be gone in the next; never quote a REST endpoint without checking whether the resource has moved to GraphQL-only.
snippets.best_practice: extend through apps/extensions, never by forking checkout: Checkout UI extensions plus Shopify Functions instead of the removed checkout.liquid; keep structured content in metaobject definitions and metafield definitions (typed, referenceable, Storefront-API readable) rather than in theme settings or app-owned storage; build theme work as Online Store 2.0 sections and blocks referenced from JSON templates, not hard-coded Liquid; read storefront data through the Storefront API with @inContext(country/language) instead of re-implementing market pricing; do bulk Admin work through bulkOperationRunQuery/bulkOperationRunMutation and respect the cost-based (leaky bucket) rate limits; keep identity in Shopify Customer Accounts unless an external IdP is contractually required.
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: which API version and which plan a feature belongs to, sunset status of checkout.liquid / Checkout Scripts / legacy REST resources, Plus-only vs. all-plan features. D2: is the named counterpart a platform feature, a Shopify-built app, or a paid third-party app - say which. D3: is it really standard, or only reachable through an app or a Function (name the Function target and the plan). D4: exact GraphQL type/connection/mutation names, metaobject and metafield modelling, checkout extension targets and their allowed capabilities, and hard platform limits (variants per product, expansion stores, webhook and API limits).
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: complex B2B (multi-level approval chains, punchout OCI/cXML, negotiated quotes, contract pricing beyond catalogs and price lists), ERP-driven customer-specific pricing and availability evaluated at request time, configurable products and CPQ, product data beyond the variant/option limits, tax and duty scenarios beyond Shopify Tax and Markets, marketplace / multi-vendor operation, deep custom checkout logic, and any data-residency or on-premise requirement.
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: checkout.liquid is removed, so every checkout customization must become a Checkout UI extension at a published target or a Shopify Function - and Functions run in WebAssembly without network access, so a live ERP call in checkout is not possible; Storefront/Admin API rate limits and cost-based throttling on catalog, inventory and price synchronisation; maturity of B2B on Shopify for approvals, quotes and punchout; per-customer pricing only via B2B catalogs/price lists rather than a live ERP price call; multi-store as Shopify Markets vs. separate expansion stores (10 included) changes the whole data and content model; no self-hosting, limited data portability, and data that lives inside a third-party app is not migratable on its own.
snippets.content_model_notes: Three separate content worlds, and a migration must say which one it targets. (1) Online Store 2.0 themes: sections/*.liquid carrying a {% schema %}, repeatable section blocks, app blocks and app embed blocks, assembled per page in JSON templates and section groups; merchants rearrange them in the theme editor, which is the out-of-the-box authoring experience. (2) Structured content: metaobject definitions and entries plus metafield definitions on products, variants, collections, customers, orders and shop - typed, referenceable, readable through the Storefront API; this is where a page-tree CMS would otherwise sit, because pages, blogs and articles are flat Online Store resources with no workflow or content versioning (staging happens by duplicating a theme) *(verify)*. (3) Checkout: checkout.liquid and Checkout Scripts are gone; only Checkout UI extensions at published extension targets and Shopify Functions can change checkout - banners, fields, validation, discount/delivery/payment logic inside sanctioned targets, not free-form markup. A headless build (Hydrogen on Oxygen, or any framework on the Storefront API) does not render Liquid sections at all: theme sections must be re-implemented as framework components, so a headless decision invalidates theme-level content work, while metaobjects and metafields survive because they are API-readable.
